# Hermes Agent FAQ & Troubleshooting Guide

---

## 1. Getting Started, UI & Observability
- **Web Dashboard:** Run `hermes dashboard` to launch the local web UI at `http://127.0.0.1:9119`. The **Chat** tab embeds the full interactive terminal TUI directly in your browser.
- **System Diagnostics:** Run `hermes doctor` to verify Python version, virtualenv, dependencies, configuration files, and authentication status.
- **Observability & Tracing:** Langfuse is bundled as an opt-in plugin. Enable it with `hermes plugins enable observability/langfuse` (or `hermes tools`) to inspect turn-by-turn execution traces, tool arguments, outputs, and latency.
- **Open WebUI Streaming:** Tool execution progress SSE events stream automatically to Open WebUI endpoints without silent callback failures.
- **Vulnerability Reporting:** Report security vulnerabilities privately via [GitHub Security Advisories](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/security/advisories/new) or by emailing `security@nousresearch.com` per `SECURITY.md`.

---

## 2. Model Providers & API Configuration
- **Local Ollama Overridden by Remote Keys:** If `provider: auto` detects remote environment variables (such as `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`), it will bypass local endpoints. Force local execution in `~/.hermes/config.yaml`:
  ```yaml
  model:
    default: ollama/your-model
    provider: custom
    base_url: http://localhost:11434
  fallback_providers: []
  ```
- **Ollama Cloud (HTTP 404):** Ollama Cloud requires standard OpenAI-compatible `/v1` routing (`https://ollama.com/v1`). Set `provider: ollama-cloud`.
- **Small Local Models (4B–9B) Running Slow:** Hermes sends the complete tool schema (~45 tools) on each turn, creating high token overhead for small models. To optimize:
  1. Disable unneeded toolsets via `hermes tools`.
  2. Use faster quantization (e.g., Q4_K_M) or upgrade to a 32B+ model.
  3. Set `terminal.backend: local` to remove container overhead.
- **Vision Support on Custom Providers:** Enable native image handling by adding `supports_vision: true` to your custom model configuration.
- **Azure AI Foundry:** Run `hermes setup` or configure `provider: azure-foundry` (auto-detects `ANTHROPIC_FOUNDRY_BASE_URL`). Claude Code-specific env variables are ignored.
- **Claude Pro/Max vs. API Token Billing:** Anthropic API keys are billed per token regardless of subscriptions. To use a Claude Pro/Max subscription allowance, authenticate via OAuth rather than an API key.
- **Google Gemini:** Legacy CLI OAuth providers have been removed. Connect using Google AI Studio via `GOOGLE_API_KEY` or `GEMINI_API_KEY`.
- **DeepSeek V4 Pricing & Normalization:** Ensure Hermes is updated so `deepseek-v4-flash` passes through directly without being normalized to `deepseek-chat` (DeepSeek V4 Pro).
- **Token Usage Tracking:** OpenAI-compatible streaming automatically passes `stream_options: {include_usage: true}` so `/usage` tracks accurate token counts on local servers (e.g., LocalAI).

---

## 3. Context, Memory & Agent Autonomy
- **Identity & Memory Files:**
  - `~/.hermes/SOUL.md`: Base agent persona, tone, instructions, and operational boundaries.
  - `~/.hermes/USER.md`: Persistent user profile, role, and personal preferences (`target="user"`).
  - `~/.hermes/MEMORY.md`: Long-term episodic memory and cross-session facts.
- **Turn Limits & Multi-Turn Goals:** Sessions default to `agent.max_turns: 90` (override for a single session using `hermes chat --max-turns <N>`). For extended autonomous work, use `/goal` to persist context across turns; resume paused tasks with `/goal resume`.
- **Context Compaction:** `ContextCompressor` automatically prunes verbose tool outputs while retaining a recent context tail. Alternative strategies can be set via `context.engine`.
- **Skill Usage Tracking:** Skill loads and edits log to `~/.hermes/skills/.usage.json`. View usage metrics with `/insights` or `hermes insights`.
- **Local Honcho Server:** Pointing `base_url` to `localhost` or `127.0.0.1` automatically injects a `"local"` placeholder API key to prevent SDK validation errors.

---

## 4. Messaging Gateways & Media Delivery
- **Interactive Gateway Setup:** Run `hermes gateway setup` to configure messaging platforms (Discord, Telegram, Slack, Matrix, etc.) via guided CLI prompts.
- **Telegram "Unauthorized User" Fix:** `allowed_chats` only filters group chats. To authorize direct messages:
  - Add your numerical Telegram user ID to `telegram.allow_from` in `config.yaml`.
  - Or DM the bot, copy the pairing code, and run `hermes pairing approve telegram <CODE>`.
  - Or set `telegram.allow_all: true` to accept all incoming messages.
- **Per-Channel Personas:** Set distinct system prompts per channel ID using the `channel_prompts` map in your platform config (supported on Discord, Telegram, Slack, Mattermost).
- **Multi-Profile Gateways:** Run multiple accounts (e.g., secondary WeChat/Telegram bots) using independent profiles or a single multiplexed gateway process with isolated sessions and credentials.
- **File & Media Transfers:** Inbound `.txt` and `.py` files are injected into context. Outbound files route automatically to Matrix (`m.file`), Telegram, and Email attachments. DingTalk delivers remote image URLs as Markdown (`![image](url)`), and MCP tool image outputs (`MEDIA:<path>`) forward directly to chat platforms.
- **Session Continuity:** Gateway restarts mark sessions as `resume_pending` to preserve chat history. Auto-resets are opt-in (`session_reset.mode: none`).

---

## 5. Extensibility & Development
- **Model Routing Policy:** Complexity-based automatic model routing (`smart_model_routing`) is unsupported by design. Configure subagent models under `delegation.provider` / `delegation.model`, or switch manually using `/model` or `hermes chat -m <model>`.
- **Subagents:** Launch parallel background tasks via the `delegate_task` tool (default concurrency: 3).
- **Custom Tools:** Build personal tools as plugins in `~/.hermes/plugins/` and enable them via `hermes plugins enable <name>`. Core built-in tools reside in `tools/` and must be exposed in `toolsets.py`.
- **Memory Plugins:** In-tree additions to `plugins/memory/` are closed. Third-party memory backends should be published as standalone plugins implementing the `MemoryProvider` ABC (`sync_turn`, `prefetch`, `shutdown`).

---

## 6. Installation & Platform Notes
- **Native Windows 10/11:** Fully supported (Tier 1) via the PowerShell installer (`install.ps1`). WSL2 is only required if using the POSIX PTY terminal pane in the web dashboard.
- **NAS & Docker Permissions:** Set `PUID` and `PGID` (or `HERMES_UID`/`HERMES_GID`) environment variables to avoid `[Errno 13] Permission denied` errors on bind mounts (`/opt/data`). Multi-arch images support `linux/amd64` and `linux/arm64` (Apple Silicon, Raspberry Pi).
- **Android (Termux):** Supported out of the box via `scripts/install.sh`, which selects the `.[termux-all]` dependency group and configures a writable `TMPDIR`.
- **Slow Updates:** Brief pauses during the Node.js update step in `hermes update` occur while Camofox silently downloads headless browser binaries.
